gloss: to massage thoroughly; to knead out; to loosen up

definitions.gloss: to massage thoroughly; to knead out (muscles); to loosen up
definitions.explanation: To rub and press a stiff muscle or knotted body part until the tension dissolves. Compound of {揉|も}む (to knead) + ほぐす (to loosen), implying both motions in one continuous action. Often used for shoulders, neck, and feet.

examples.japanese: {固|かた}くなった{筋肉|きんにく}を{丁寧|ていねい}にもみほぐした。
examples.english: I carefully massaged the stiffened muscles loose.

examples.japanese: {試合|しあい}の{前|まえ}にトレーナーが{選手|せんしゅ}の{足|あし}をしっかりもみほぐしてくれた。
examples.english: Before the match the trainer thoroughly massaged the athlete's legs.

notes:
Transitive godan verb (もみほぐす・もみほぐして・もみほぐした). Compound of {揉|も}む + ほぐす, common in massage and sports contexts.

TRANSITIVITY:
Transitive: marks the body part with を.
- {肩|かた}をもみほぐす: to massage shoulders
- {足|あし}をもみほぐす: to massage feet

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {肩|かた}・{首|くび}・{腰|こし}をもみほぐす: to massage shoulders/neck/lower back
- {筋肉|きんにく}をもみほぐす: to loosen the muscles
- {凝|こ}りをもみほぐす: to knead out stiffness

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {揉|も}む: to knead; to rub — broader, may not imply loosening as the goal
- ほぐす: to loosen; to untangle — broader; not limited to massage
- マッサージする: to massage — generic loanword, doesn't specify kneading motion
